### Kinsale Capital Group Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results


October 22, 2026


RICHMOND, Va.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Kinsale Capital Group, Inc. (NYSE: KNSL) reported net income of $98.1 million, $4.36 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026 compared to $141.6 million, $6.09 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025. Net income was $386.6 million, $16.97 per diluted share, for the first nine months of 2026 compared to $365.0 million, $15.67 per diluted share, for the first nine months of 2025. Net income included after-tax catastrophe losses of $1.7 million in the third quarter of 2026 and $1.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. Net income included after-tax catastrophe losses of $7.2 million in the first nine months of 2026 and $21.7 million in the first nine months of 2025.


Net operating earnings(1) were $128.3 million, $5.70 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026 compared to $121.2 million, $5.21 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025. Net operating earnings(1) were $372.3 million, $16.34 per diluted share, for the first nine months of 2026 compared to $319.0 million, $13.70 per diluted share, for the first nine months of 2025.

Highlights for the quarter included:


- Gross written premiums decreased by 4.8% to $462.9 million, and net written premiums decreased by 1.5% to $399.1 million
- Net earned premiums increased by 3.0% to $423.5 million
- Net investment income increased by 17.5% to $58.3 million
- Underwriting income (2) was $107.1 million, resulting in a combined ratio (5) of 75.4%
- Annualized return on equity (6) was 26.6% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026
- Annualized operating return on equity (7) was 25.6% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026
- Net income includes a $37.6 million pre-tax realized loss on the sale of fixed-maturity securities due to a strategic repositioning of the investment portfolio expected to improve long-term returns


"Our underwriting results this quarter demonstrate discipline in a competitive market," said Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer, Michael P. Kehoe. "We continue to produce exceptional underwriting margins and strong investment income which allows us to return capital to stockholders. Disciplined underwriting and technology-enabled low costs remain the foundation of our strategy to create long-term value for our stockholders."


**Results of Operations**


*Underwriting Results*


Gross written premiums were $462.9 million for the third quarter of 2026 compared to $486.3 million for the third quarter of 2025, a decrease of 4.8%. Gross written premiums were $1,472.5 million for the first nine months of 2026 compared to $1,526.0 million for the first nine months of 2025, a decrease of 3.5%. The decrease in gross written premiums was primarily due to heightened competition in the Company's property divisions, where premiums declined 19.3% and 18.7% in the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, including declines of 26.8% and 29.8% in the Commercial Property Division. Gross written premiums in the Company's casualty business increased 0.9% for the third quarter of 2026 and 3.0% for the first nine months of 2026 compared to the prior-year periods, primarily due to an increase in bound accounts offset in part by a change in business mix towards smaller accounts.


Underwriting income(2) was $107.1 million, resulting in a combined ratio(5) of 75.4% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $105.7 million and a combined ratio(5) of 74.9% for the third quarter of 2025. The increase in underwriting income(2) was largely due to growth in net earned premiums and higher favorable development of loss reserves from prior accident years offset in part by lower ceding commissions as a result of increased retention on the Company's reinsurance treaties. Loss(3) and expense(4) ratios were 53.4% and 22.0%, respectively, for the third quarter of 2026 compared to 53.9% and 21.0% for the third quarter of 2025.


Underwriting income(2) was $307.0 million, resulting in a combined ratio(5) of 76.1% for the first nine months of 2026 compared to $268.6 million and a combined ratio(5) of 77.5% for the first nine months of 2025. The increase in underwriting income(2) was largely due to growth in net earned premiums, lower catastrophe losses and higher favorable development of loss reserves from prior accident years. Loss(3) and expense(4) ratios were 54.5% and 21.6%, respectively, for the first nine months of 2026 compared to 56.9% and 20.6% for the first nine months of 2025. The loss ratio for the first nine months of 2025 included 2.3 points of net catastrophe losses, primarily related to the Palisades Fire.


The increase in the expense ratio for both the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 compared to the prior-year periods was primarily due to lower ceding commissions as a result of higher retention on the Company’s reinsurance treaties. The economic effect of lower ceding commissions was more than offset by the retention of incremental underwriting margin and higher investment income.

*Investment Results*


Net investment income was $58.3 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $49.6 million in the third quarter of 2025, an increase of 17.5%. Net investment income was $169.4 million in the first nine months of 2026 compared to $139.9 million in the first nine months of 2025, an increase of 21.1%. These increases were driven by growth in the Company's investment portfolio generated largely from the investment of strong operating cash flows. The Company’s investment portfolio had an annualized gross investment return(8) of 4.4% and 4.3% for the first nine months of 2026 and 2025, respectively. Funds are generally invested conservatively in high-quality securities with an average credit quality of "AA-" and the weighted average duration of the fixed-maturity investment portfolio, including cash equivalents, was 4.4 years and 4.0 years at September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, respectively. Cash and invested assets totaled $5.5 billion at September 30, 2026 and $5.2 billion at December 31, 2025.


During the third quarter of 2026, the Company repositioned a portion of its investment portfolio to improve expected long-term returns. The Company sold certain common stock holdings in a gain position and reinvested the proceeds in higher conviction common stock investments. The Company simultaneously sold lower-yielding fixed-maturity securities in a largely offsetting loss position and reinvested the proceeds in higher-yielding fixed-maturity investments. The repositioning reduced third quarter pre-tax earnings by $37.6 million as the equity gains were recorded through earnings in the period of appreciation and the bond losses were recorded through earnings upon sale. There was no impact to book value.


(8)


Gross investment return is investment income from fixed-maturity and equity securities (and short-term investments, if any), before any deductions for fees and expenses, expressed as a percentage of average beginning and ending book values of those investments during the period.


*Capital Return to Stockholders*


During the third quarter of 2026, the Company repurchased 269,004 shares of its common stock in the open market at an average price of $371.74 per share for a total cost of $100.0 million. At September 30, 2026, the Company had $237.5 million of capacity remaining under its share repurchase program. In the aggregate, the Company has repurchased 990,763 shares of its common stock for a total cost of $362.5 million.


During the third quarter of 2026, the Company declared and paid a cash dividend of $0.25 per share of common stock for a total distribution of $5.6 million.


*Other*


The effective tax rates for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025 were 20.0% and 20.6%, respectively. In the first nine months of 2026 and 2025, the effective tax rates were lower than the federal statutory rate of 21% primarily due to the tax benefits from stock-based compensation, including stock options exercised, and from tax-exempt investment income.


Stockholders' equity was $1.9 billion at September 30, 2026 and $2.0 billion at December 31, 2025. Book value per share was $85.25 at September 30, 2026 compared to $84.66 at December 31, 2025. Annualized operating return on equity(7) was 25.6% for the first nine months of 2026, an increase from 25.4% for the first nine months of 2025. The increase was due primarily to higher profitability compared to the prior-year period offset in part by higher average stockholders' equity.


**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


*Net Operating Earnings*


Net operating earnings is defined as net income excluding the effects of the change in the fair value of equity securities, after taxes, net realized investment gains and losses, after taxes, and change in allowance for credit losses on investments, after taxes. Management believes the exclusion of these items provides a useful comparison of the Company's underlying business performance from period to period. Net operating earnings and percentages or calculations using net operating earnings (e.g., diluted operating earnings per share and annualized operating return on equity) are non-GAAP financial measures. Net operating earnings should not be viewed as a substitute for net income calculated in accordance with GAAP, and other companies may define net operating earnings differently.
